extracted.intended_audience: applicants, patent and trademark attorneys, and legal practitioners dealing with Turkish industrial property (trademarks, patents, designs, utility models)
extracted.subtask_description: English translation of the Turkish Industrial Property Code setting out legal standards for trademarks, geographical indications, designs, patents and utility models, including application, examination, rights, refusals, priority, and procedural rules. This page provides statutory criteria and procedural requirements used to evaluate and process IP filings and disputes in Turkey.

rubrics_metrics.name: Purpose and scope of the Code
rubrics_metrics.description: The Code's purpose is to protect rights relating to trademark, geographical signs, design, patent, utility model and traditional product names and to encompass applications, registrations and post-registration processes and legal/criminal sanctions concerning violation of these rights.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Governs procedural and substantive matters across trademarks, geographical indications, designs, patents, utility models and related enforcement; used as the statutory basis for processing and adjudicating IP matters in Turkey.

rubrics_metrics.name: Persons entitled to protection
rubrics_metrics.description: Those who may benefit from protection include: Turkish citizens; natural or legal persons domiciled or engaged in industrial or commercial activities in Turkey; persons entitled under the Paris Convention/WTO Agreement; and persons from states providing reciprocity to Turkish citizens.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Eligibility for filing and protection is limited to the above classes; this affects who may apply or enforce rights under the Code.

rubrics_metrics.name: What may constitute a trademark
rubrics_metrics.description: Trademarks may consist of any signs like words (including personal names), figures, colours, letters, numbers, sounds and the shape of goods or their packaging, provided they are capable of distinguishing goods/services and can be represented on the register clearly and precisely.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Marks must be capable of graphical/other representation sufficient to determine the precise subject matter of protection; includes non-traditional signs (sound, shape, colour) if they meet distinctiveness/representation requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Absolute grounds for refusal — lack of distinctive character
rubrics_metrics.description: Signs which are devoid of any distinctive character shall not be registered as trademarks.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a sign cannot distinguish one undertaking's goods/services from another's, it is absolutely unregistrable unless acquired distinctiveness through use (see guidance on acquired distinctiveness).

rubrics_metrics.name: Absolute grounds for refusal — purely descriptive signs
rubrics_metrics.description: Signs which consist exclusively or include as an essential element indications which serve in trade to designate kind, type, characteristics, quality, quantity, intended purpose, value, geographical origin, time of production or other characteristics of goods/services shall not be registered.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Descriptive/indicative terms that traders need to use in commerce are refused registration to avoid monopolization of common descriptive language.

rubrics_metrics.name: Absolute grounds for refusal — signs identical or indistinguishably similar to earlier marks
rubrics_metrics.description: Signs identical to or indistinguishably similar to a trademark already registered or applied for, relating to identical goods/services or goods/services of identical type, shall not be registered.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prevents identical/near-identical marks for the same types of goods/services; relates to absolute examination under Article 5.

rubrics_metrics.name: Absolute grounds for refusal — signs used by everyone / denoting a group
rubrics_metrics.description: Signs which consist exclusively or include as an essential element signs or indications used by everyone in trade or serving to distinguish members of a particular professional, vocational or commercial group from others shall not be registered.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Common trade signs and membership descriptors are blocked from private appropriation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Absolute grounds for refusal — shapes/characteristics from nature or giving technical result or substantial value
rubrics_metrics.description: Signs which consist exclusively of the shape or another characteristic which results from the nature of the goods themselves, or which is mandatory to obtain a technical result, or gives substantial value to the goods shall not be registered.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Protects functional shapes and shapes that materially add value from being monopolized as trademarks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Absolute grounds for refusal — deceptive signs
rubrics_metrics.description: Signs which would deceive the public, for instance as to the nature, quality or geographical origin of the goods or service, shall not be registered.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prevents misleading marks that could deceive consumers about product characteristics or origin.

rubrics_metrics.name: Absolute grounds for refusal — Article 6ter emblems and related signs
rubrics_metrics.description: Signs refused pursuant to Article 6ter of the Paris Convention (e.g., state emblems, official signs) shall not be registered.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Internationally-protected emblems and official signs cannot be registered as trademarks in line with Paris Convention obligations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Absolute grounds for refusal — public interest / historical / cultural emblems
rubrics_metrics.description: Signs other than those covered by Article 6ter but which are of public interest and contain historical, cultural values, emblems, badges or escutcheons for which competent authority consent is not given shall not be registered.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Protects public/cultural symbols from private trademark appropriation unless authorized.

rubrics_metrics.name: Absolute grounds for refusal — religious symbols
rubrics_metrics.description: Signs that contain religious values or symbols shall not be registered.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prevents registration of marks that include religious symbols, protecting public sensitivities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Absolute grounds for refusal — contrary to public policy or morality
rubrics_metrics.description: Signs which are contrary to public policy or accepted principles of morality shall not be registered.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Marks offensive to public order or morality are excluded from registration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Absolute grounds for refusal — contains registered geographical sign
rubrics_metrics.description: Signs which consist of a registered geographical sign or which contain a registered geographical sign shall not be registered as a trademark.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prevents conflict between trademarks and protected geographical indications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acquired distinctiveness / proof to overcome absolute refusals
rubrics_metrics.description: If a trademark has been used before the application and has acquired distinctive character through this use for the applied goods/services, registration may not be refused under the listed absolute grounds (e.g., lack of distinctiveness, descriptiveness).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants may overcome absolute refusals by proving acquired distinctiveness via use; procedural rules (e.g., evidence) are governed by regulation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consent can cure certain relative objections
rubrics_metrics.description: A trademark application may not be refused under certain relative grounds if a notarial document showing clear consent of the prior trademark proprietor is submitted; procedures for consent are determined by regulation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A prior proprietor's explicit consent (properly documented) can remove an otherwise blocking earlier right.

rubrics_metrics.name: Relative grounds for refusal — likelihood of confusion/association
rubrics_metrics.description: An application shall be refused upon opposition if there exists a likelihood of confusion, including likelihood of association, due to identity or similarity of signs and identity or similarity of goods/services.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Standard confusion test between earlier rights and applied-for mark considering similarity of sign and goods/services and public perception.

rubrics_metrics.name: Relative grounds for refusal — agent/representative filed without proprietor's consent
rubrics_metrics.description: A trademark application filed by a commercial agent or representative in his own name without the proprietor's consent and without justifiable ground shall be refused upon opposition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Protects proprietors against agents registering marks in their own name absent consent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Relative grounds for refusal — prior unregistered marks/used signs
rubrics_metrics.description: If a right to a non-registered trademark or another sign used in the course of trade was acquired prior to the application date or priority date, the application shall be refused upon opposition of that prior proprietor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recognises unregistered (prior) trade use as enforceable against later applications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Relative grounds for refusal — well-known marks (Article 6bis)
rubrics_metrics.description: Trademark applications identical or similar to well-known marks shall be refused upon opposition in respect of identical and similar goods/services.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Protects fame-based rights even across classes where confusion may not be present.

rubrics_metrics.name: Relative grounds for refusal — reputation/dilution regardless of dissimilar goods
rubrics_metrics.description: An application identical or similar to an earlier registered trademark may be refused even for dissimilar goods/services where use without due cause would take unfair advantage of, or be detrimental to, the distinctive character or repute of the earlier mark due to its reputation in Turkey.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Dilution/reputation protection extends to dissimilar goods where confusion is not necessary but reputation is harmed or unfair advantage is taken.

rubrics_metrics.name: Relative grounds for refusal — use of another's name, trade name or IP
rubrics_metrics.description: Applications shall be refused upon opposition if they consist of a person's name, trade name, photograph, copyright or any other intellectual property right of another person.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prevents registration of marks that incorporate the protected IP or personal rights of third parties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Temporal post-expiry protection — collective/guarantee marks (3-year rule)
rubrics_metrics.description: An application identical or similar to a collective or guarantee mark filed within three years after its protection expired due to non-renewal shall be refused upon opposition of the previous right holder.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides a limited post-expiry protection period for collective/guarantee marks if not renewed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Temporal post-expiry protection — registered marks (2-year rule when used)
rubrics_metrics.description: An application identical or similar to a registered trademark filed within two years following expiry due to non-renewal shall be refused upon opposition provided the trademark has been used during that period.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Limited grace period protects previously-used marks shortly after non-renewal if they continue to be used.

rubrics_metrics.name: Relative grounds for refusal — bad faith applications
rubrics_metrics.description: Trademark applications filed in bad faith shall be refused upon opposition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Bad faith grounds are a basis for refusal; bad faith may be shown by circumstances surrounding filing/use.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acquisition of trademark protection by registration
rubrics_metrics.description: Trademark protection is acquired by registration; rights arising from registration are granted exclusively to the trademark proprietor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Registration is the primary basis of enforceable rights; proprietors may bring actions to prevent unauthorised uses as set out in the Code.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope of proprietor's rights and prohibited acts
rubrics_metrics.description: The proprietor may prohibit (a) use of identical sign on covered goods/services; (b) use of identical/similar sign causing likelihood of confusion (including association); (c) use of identical/similar sign that takes unfair advantage of or is detrimental to the mark's distinctive character or repute. Prohibited acts include affixing sign to goods/packaging, putting goods on market, importing/exporting under the sign, using sign on business papers/advertisements, using as domain name/router code/keyword with commercial impression when no right, using as trade or company name, and comparative advertising contrary to law.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Enumerates the substantive acts the proprietor can stop; includes online uses (domain names, keywords).

rubrics_metrics.name: Effective date of rights and provisional compensation remedies
rubrics_metrics.description: Rights conferred by trademark take effect against third parties as of the publication date of registration. The applicant (pre-registration) may institute proceedings for compensation for acts occurring after publication of the application (Bulletin) where those acts would later be prohibited; courts may not decide on validity claims raised before registration is published.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Publication of application confers limited provisional protection enabling compensation claims, but validity disputes are constrained prior to registration publication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exceptions — honest use
rubrics_metrics.description: Trademark proprietor may not prevent honest use of the trademark by third parties in trade in forms including: natural persons indicating their own name/address; making descriptive explanations concerning the goods/services; situations necessary to indicate intended purpose of a product (e.g., accessories, spare parts).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Carves out fair descriptive and nominative uses that would otherwise be prohibited by exclusive rights.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of registered trademark in reference works
rubrics_metrics.description: If a registered trademark is published in a dictionary, encyclopedia or similar reference work without indication that it is registered and giving impression it is the generic name, the publisher must correct by indicating registration or remove the trademark (immediately for electronic, at first printed edition after request).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Protects proprietors from loss of distinctiveness via incorrect reference work entries; imposes corrective obligation on publishers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Revocation for non-use (5-year rule)
rubrics_metrics.description: If within five years following registration the trademark has not been put to genuine use in Turkey for the goods/services for which it is registered, or use has been suspended for an uninterrupted five-year period, the trademark shall be revoked unless there are proper reasons for non-use.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use requirement limits monopolies on unused marks; certain forms of use (variations not altering distinctiveness, export-only use) count as genuine use.

rubrics_metrics.name: What constitutes 'use' for non-use assessment
rubrics_metrics.description: Use includes use with different elements not altering distinctive character, use on goods/packaging solely for export purposes, and use by third parties with consent of proprietor counts as proprietor's use.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clarifies evidentiary standards for demonstrating genuine use to resist revocation for non-use.

rubrics_metrics.name: Remedies regarding marks registered in the agent's/representative's name
rubrics_metrics.description: If an identical or indistinguishably similar trademark is registered in the name of the agent/representative without the proprietor's consent (and absent justifiable reason), the proprietor may seek in court prohibition of use and request transfer of the registration to himself.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides remedy for registrations made by agents/representatives in bad faith or without consent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Trademark application content and required documents
rubrics_metrics.description: An application must include: application form with applicant identity; representation of trademark; list of goods/services; proof fee paid; technical specifications for collective/guarantee marks; proof of priority fee payment if claimed; transliteration into Latin alphabet if letters other than Latin used.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Only one trademark per application; classification per Nice Agreement; applicant may divide application; spelling/obvious mistakes may be corrected; regulatory details determined by regulation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Classification and similarity of goods/services
rubrics_metrics.description: Goods/services must be classified according to the Nice Classification. Goods/services are not presumed similar because in same class nor dissimilar because in different classes; Office may correct classes/numbers as needed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Classification is procedural but does not determinatively establish similarity; substantive similarity assessment remains independent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Division of applications and correction of errors
rubrics_metrics.description: An application may be divided into two or more applications (by goods/services) until registration; spelling mistakes and obvious mistakes that do not change content may be corrected upon request.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Enables procedural flexibility for applicants to split applications or correct non-substantive errors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Priority right — who and time limits
rubrics_metrics.description: Nationals of Paris Convention/WTO member states or persons domiciled/operating there enjoy priority for filing in Turkey within six months following initial filing for identical goods/services; supporting priority certificate from competent authority is mandatory; failure to use within period forfeits priority.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Also includes provisions for exhibition-based priority, first-to-file among simultaneous exhibitors, and rules for multiple priority claims (earliest valid priority date governs).

rubrics_metrics.name: Claiming priority — procedural requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicant must state the priority right with the application and deposit the fee; if priority certificate is not submitted within three months the priority request is deemed not made.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Procedural timing is strict; fees and documentary proof required to preserve priority.

rubrics_metrics.name: International (Madrid Protocol) applications treated as domestic filing
rubrics_metrics.description: International applications under the Madrid Protocol shall have the same results as an application filed directly to the Office, deemed filed at first hour and minute of international application date; in case of same date, smaller international registration number deemed earlier.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: National effects and interplays with national applications are specified; fees for Office proceedings under Madrid are set by communiqué.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedural/formal examination and defects (application date effects)
rubrics_metrics.description: Office formally examines conformity with Articles 3 and 11. If no deficiencies, the application finalizes at date/hour/minute of reception. If deficiencies exist, applicant given two months to remedy. Deficiencies related to applicant identity, representation, list of goods/services and proof of fee affect application date until remedied; other deficiencies (e.g., collective mark technical specs, priority fee, transliteration) do not affect application date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Failure to remedy deficiencies in time causes cancellation; if fee for some classes unpaid, application is examined for paid classes only; failure to remedy priority defects causes loss of priority right.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examination for absolute grounds and publication
rubrics_metrics.description: If the Office finds no formal deficiencies it examines the application under absolute grounds (Article 5). If some/all goods/services cannot be registered, application refused for those items. Applications that fulfill conditions and are not refused shall be published in the Bulletin. Refusal decisions after publication are also published.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Two-stage process: formal examination -> substantive absolute grounds -> publication; publication triggers opposition windows and provisional effects.
